stories.headline: Americans vote in midterms seen as a test of Trump
body: US voters went to the polls on Tuesday in midterm elections widely seen as a referendum on Donald Trump's presidency.
Control of Congress is at stake; the first results come after polls begin closing at 23:00 GMT.
Final results may take days, and Missouri voters also decide on abortion and transgender measures.
stories.joke: Results tonight, recounts this week, arguments forever.
stories.vc: Which party controls Congress shapes US tariffs, tech rules and AI policy, all of which move global markets.

stories.headline: Trump says the US will stop paying Israel after this year
body: Trump said he and Netanyahu agreed months ago that US funding to Israel, which he put at $4 billion a year, will stop after this year.
He added that the US would still help Israel 'if they need it'.
It was not clear what kind of aid he meant.
stories.joke: A $4 billion line item, cancelled on breakfast TV.
stories.vc: A change in US military aid would reshape Israel's defence budget and its arms industry's export push.

stories.headline: Greenland approves a security deal with the US and Denmark
body: Greenland's parliament approved a security pact with Denmark and the US by 16 votes to 0, with seven abstaining.
It aims to boost security in the Arctic and North Atlantic.
The deal follows months of tension over Trump's threats to take the island.
stories.joke: From 'we'll buy it' to 'let's sign a pact'. Progress.
stories.vc: Arctic security deals open the door to minerals and shipping-route investment in Greenland.

stories.headline: India lifted nearly 500 million people out of extreme poverty
body: India's extreme poverty fell from 27.1% to 2.6% between 2011 and 2023, a new World Bank report says.
That's nearly 500 million people, a scale only China has matched, over 40 years.
But income and wealth inequality has widened since the 1990s, the World Inequality Report says.
stories.vc: A fast-growing lower-middle class is India's biggest consumer story, though inequality limits how far it spreads.

stories.headline: Sensex jumps another 1,225 points; Nifty nears 23,800
body: The Sensex rose 1,225 points on Tuesday, and the Nifty gained 370 points to 23,811.
It was the fourth straight day of gains.
Falling crude oil prices and foreign fund inflows drove the rally.
stories.joke: Four green days in a row. Investors are suspicious of their own luck.
stories.vc: Cheaper oil helps India's import bill and inflation, and foreign money returning lifts IPO hopes.

stories.headline: Karnataka tech startups raised $4.6B this year, up 26%
body: Karnataka tech companies raised $4.6 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 26% from $3.7 billion, Tracxn says.
That reverses a 40% fall in the same period last year.
But the number of funding rounds fell 35% to 397, so money is concentrating in fewer firms.
stories.joke: More money, fewer cheques. VCs are picking favourites.
stories.vc: Concentrated funding means bigger rounds for winners and a harder climb for early-stage Bengaluru founders.

stories.headline: Palantir's revenue nearly doubles, but a warning sign hides inside
body: Palantir's quarterly revenue grew 96% to $2.31 billion, its first quarter above $2 billion.
It beat forecasts, but its enterprise sales, the big growth area, showed signs of slowing.
The stock traded slightly lower on Tuesday.
stories.joke: Doubling revenue and still getting side-eye. Tough crowd.
stories.vc: When a hot stock beats forecasts and still slips, investors are pricing in perfection, a warning for AI valuations.

stories.headline: Anthropic's compute costs are eating more of its revenue
body: An updated IPO filing shows Anthropic's quarterly revenue hit $17 billion, up from $11.5 billion.
But compute now takes 58% of revenue, up from 48%, and its compute bill reached $10 billion for the quarter.
Revenue per compute dollar fell from just over 2x to 1.72x.
stories.joke: Selling AI is great. Paying for the chips is the hard part.
stories.vc: Compute margins are the number IPO investors will watch most; they decide whether AI labs can ever be very profitable.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike buys two AI security startups for about $500M
body: CrowdStrike is buying Fiddler AI for about $400 million and Dreadnode for about $95 million, the WSJ reports.
Fiddler monitors AI agents inside companies; Dreadnode tests AI apps for security flaws.
Demand to secure AI agents is rising fast as firms roll them out.
stories.joke: Step one: build AI agents. Step two: hire someone to watch them.
stories.vc: AI-agent security is becoming its own market, a quick exit route for startups in the space.

stories.headline: AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B
body: Fal, which runs AI video, image and audio models for customers, raised $1.3 billion led by Bessemer.
Nvidia, Sound Ventures and T. Rowe Price joined; it was worth $8 billion in April.
Demand for inference, running trained models, is soaring.
stories.joke: Doubling your valuation in seven months: the AI version of a quiet year.
stories.vc: Inference is where AI spending is moving; platforms that run models cheaply are the new picks and shovels.

stories.headline: Ballistic Ventures seeks $490M for AI-era security bets
body: Ted Schlein's Ballistic Ventures filed to raise $490 million across two new funds.
That includes a $360 million flagship fund, matching its last one, and a $130 million Fund B.
AI is driving a new wave of cybersecurity spending.
stories.joke: Every AI breakthrough comes with a free security problem.
stories.vc: Specialist VC funds raising steadily shows cybersecurity is one of the most reliable AI-era bets.

stories.headline: Why Republican women lag Democrats in running and winning
body: Marsha Blackburn is poised to become Tennessee's first woman governor in its 230-year history.
A record number of women are running for the US House this year, according to CAWP.
But The 19th says Republicans have a weaker pipeline for women candidates and are reluctant to fix it.
stories.vc: Parties that recruit more women widen their talent pool; the gap affects who shapes policy on care and work.

stories.headline: AMU women students ask the Education Minister for voting rights
body: Students of Aligarh Muslim University's Women's College asked the Union Education Minister to help them vote in the student union election on 5 November.
The Hindu reported over 4,000 women students lacked voting rights in the main AMU union poll.
AMU denies this, saying they vote in their own Women's College union election the same day.
stories.vc: Student politics is often where women's political careers start, so who gets a vote matters early.

stories.headline: Epstein survivors urge voters to reject broken promises
body: Some Jeffrey Epstein survivors who voted for Trump to get the Epstein files released are now urging voters to reject him.
Jena-Lisa Jones says she backed Trump only because of that promise.
Survivors have been working to turn out voters in Florida and beyond.
stories.vc: Survivor-led campaigns show how accountability for abuse has become a voting issue.

stories.headline: AHH opens a kidney and urology hospital in Bhubaneswar
body: Asia Healthcare Holdings has opened a super-speciality uro-nephrology hospital in Bhubaneswar, part of a ₹100 crore Odisha expansion.
It is the 8th centre of its Asian Institute of Nephrology and Urology (AINU).
AHH aims to run 10 hospitals by the end of this financial year.
stories.vc: Single-specialty chains like this are a fast-growing, PE-backed corner of Indian healthcare.

stories.headline: AIIMS Rajkot opens a ₹39 crore cancer radiotherapy unit
body: Health Minister J.P. Nadda opened a ₹39 crore advanced radiotherapy facility at AIIMS Rajkot.
It will improve cancer care for Rajkot and the wider Saurashtra region.
It was set up under the PMSSY scheme to fix regional gaps in specialist care.
stories.vc: Public cancer units outside metros cut travel costs for patients and ease pressure on big-city hospitals.

stories.headline: Gut Clinic opens three new centres across Delhi-NCR
body: Gut Clinic, a gastroenterology and liver care network, opened centres in Lajpat Nagar, Gurugram and New Friends Colony.
It focuses on outpatient specialist care closer to patients' homes.
The centres were set up with CliniShare.
stories.vc: Outpatient-only specialist chains need far less capital than hospitals, so they can expand quickly.

stories.headline: Haas drops Ocon for good; Rafa Camara debuts in Brazil
body: Haas says Esteban Ocon will not race for the team again after strained relations and a heated row in Mexico.
Brazilian Rafa Camara, signed for 2027, will make his F1 debut this weekend at his home Grand Prix.
Team boss Ayao Komatsu made the call to bench Ocon.
stories.joke: A home-race debut. No pressure, Rafa.
stories.vc: A Brazilian rookie at Interlagos is a marketing win for Haas and F1's South American sponsors.
